fanoutqa_039399.x:
Peregrine falcon :: Ecology and behaviour :: Speed :: chunk_0011
A study testing the flight physics of an "ideal falcon" found a theoretical speed limit at 400 km/h (250 mph) for low-altitude flight and 625 km/h (388 mph) for high-altitude flight.[[59]](#cite_note-Tucker1998-64) Some sources state that the peregrine falcon can reach over 320 km/h (200 mph) during its stoop,[[19]](#cite_note-USFWS-19) which would make it the [fastest animal](/wiki/Fastest_animals "Fastest animals") on the planet.[[60]](#cite_note-BBC-65)[[61]](#cite_note-Smithsonian-66)[[62]](#cite_note-67) According to a *[National Geographic](/wiki/National_Geographic_(U.S._TV_channel) "National Geographic (U.S. TV channel)")* TV program, in 2005 Ken Franklin recorded a falcon stooping at a top speed of 389 km/h (242 mph).[[63]](#cite_note-Harpole2005-68)[[64]](#cite_note-TerminalVelocity-69) Other sources state that radar tracks have never confirmed these kinds of speeds, with the highest reliably measured being 184 km/h (114 mph).[[65]](#cite_note-Journal_of_Aviation_Biology-70)

Common symptoms of breast cancer

Most people with breast cancer have no symptoms at the time of diagnosis; a breast cancer screening test detects their tumor.[[22]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHayesLippman2022"Evaluation_of_Breast_Masses"-22) For those who do have symptoms, a new [lump](/wiki/Breast_lump "Breast lump") in the breast is most common. Most breast lumps are not cancerous, though lumps that are painless, hard, and with irregular edges are more likely to be cancerous.[[23]](#cite_note-ACS-SS-23) Other symptoms include skin thickening known as [peau d'orange](/wiki/Peau_d%27orange "Peau d'orange")[[24]](#cite_note-24) swelling or pain in the breast; dimpling, thickening, redness, or dryness of the breast skin; and pain, or inversion of the nipple.[[23]](#cite_note-ACS-SS-23) Some may experience unusual discharge from the breasts, or swelling of the lymph nodes under the arms or along the [collar bone](/wiki/Collar_bone "Collar bone").[[23]](#cite_note-ACS-SS-23)

Some less common forms of breast cancer cause distinctive symptoms. Up to 5% of people with breast cancer have [inflammatory breast cancer](/wiki/Inflammatory_breast_cancer "Inflammatory breast cancer"), where cancer cells block the [lymph vessels](/wiki/Lymph_vessel "Lymph vessel") of one breast, causing the breast to swell substantially and redden over three to six months.[[25]](#cite_note-25) Up to 3% of people with breast cancer have [Paget's disease of the breast](/wiki/Paget%27s_disease_of_the_breast "Paget's disease of the breast"), with [eczema](/wiki/Eczema "Eczema")-like red, scaly irritation on the

Upon release, "Easy on Me" achieved success on streaming platforms. It became the [most streamed song](/wiki/List_of_most-streamed_songs_on_Spotify "List of most-streamed songs on Spotify") on [Spotify](/wiki/Spotify "Spotify"), both in a day[[d]](#cite_note-79) and a single week.[[e]](#cite_note-81)[[77]](#cite_note-variety.com-82) In the United Kingdom, "Easy on Me" opened with 3.2 million Spotify streams, the most received by any song in a day.[[77]](#cite_note-variety.com-82) It also broke the record for the most streamed song in a single week in the country, with 24 million streams.[[78]](#cite_note-OfficialStreams-83) On [Amazon Music](/wiki/Amazon_Music "Amazon Music"), it earned the most first-day streams globally and the most first-day [Alexa](/wiki/Amazon_Alexa "Amazon Alexa") requests for any song in the platform's history.[[79]](#cite_note-84) "Easy on Me" debuted at number 195 on the [*Billboard* Global 200](/wiki/Billboard_Global_200 "Billboard Global 200") with just five hours of tracking and became Adele's first song to reach the chart's summit the following week. That week, it sold 136,300 downloads, the third-largest sales week for any song on that chart, and earned 178.2 million streams, the second-largest streaming week. It also became the second number one song in history to double the chart points of the number two.[[80]](#cite_note-85)

In the United States, "Easy on Me" debuted at number 68 on the [*Billboard* Hot 100](/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") with its first five hours of tracking.[[81]](#cite_note-86) The following week, it became Adele's fifth chart-topping single. The stadiums for the 2023–24 season show a large disparity in capacity. For example, [Old Trafford](/wiki/Old_Trafford "Old Trafford"), the home of [Manchester United](/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C."), has a capacity of 74,031 whilst [Dean Court](/wiki/Dean_Court "Dean Court"), the home of [Bournemouth](/wiki/AFC_Bournemouth "AFC Bournemouth"), has a capacity of 11,307. The main campus consists of more than 200 buildings on 600 acres (2.4 km2) in Princeton, New Jersey.[[6]](#cite_note-Princeton-About-6) The James Forrestal Campus, a smaller location designed mainly as a research and instruction complex, is split between nearby [Plainsboro](/wiki/Plainsboro_Township,_New_Jersey "Plainsboro Township, New Jersey") and [South Brunswick](/wiki/South_Brunswick,_New_Jersey "South Brunswick, New Jersey"). The campuses are situated about one hour from both New York City and Philadelphia on the train.[[165]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFiskeLecuyer2019567-168) The university also owns more than 520 acres (2.1 km2) of property in [West Windsor Township](/wiki/West_Windsor_Township,_New_Jersey "West Windsor Township, New Jersey"),[[6]](#cite_note-Princeton-About-6) and is where Princeton is planning to construct a graduate student housing complex, which will be known as "Lake Campus North".[[166]](#cite_note-169)

The first building on campus was Nassau Hall, completed in 1756, and situated on the northern edge of the campus facing Nassau Street.[[167]]

A member of the Japanese COVID-19 Advisory Committee on the basic action policy co-authored a *[British Medical Journal](/wiki/The_BMJ "The BMJ")* editorial, which stated, "holding Tokyo 2020 for domestic political and economic purposes—ignoring scientific and moral imperatives—is contradictory to Japan's commitment to global health and human security".[[52]](#cite_note-BMJ373n962-60)

fanoutqa_009447.x:
Earth :: Surface environment :: part 02 :: chunk_0015
The land surface and the [ocean floor](/wiki/Ocean_floor "Ocean floor") form the top of [Earth's crust](/wiki/Earth%27s_crust "Earth's crust"), which together with parts of the [upper mantle](/wiki/Upper_mantle_(Earth) "Upper mantle (Earth)") form [Earth's lithosphere](/wiki/Lithosphere#Earth's_lithosphere "Lithosphere"). Earth's crust may be divided into [oceanic](/wiki/Oceanic_crust "Oceanic crust") and [continental](/wiki/Continental_crust "Continental crust") crust. Beneath the ocean-floor sediments, the oceanic crust is predominantly [basaltic](/wiki/Basalt "Basalt"), while the continental crust may include lower density materials such as [granite](/wiki/Granite "Granite"), sediments and metamorphic rocks.[[125]](#cite_note-layers_earth-133) Nearly 75% of the continental surfaces are covered by sedimentary rocks, although they form about 5% of the mass of the crust.[[126]](#cite_note-jessey-134)

Earth's surface [topography](/wiki/Topography "Topography") comprises both the [topography of the ocean surface](/wiki/Ocean_surface_topography "Ocean surface topography"), and the [shape](/wiki/Hypsometry "Hypsometry") of Earth's land surface. The [terrain](/wiki/Terrain "Terrain") of the land surface varies greatly and consists of mountains, [deserts](/wiki/Desert "Desert"), [plains](/wiki/Plain "Plain"), [plateaus](/wiki/Plateau "Plateau"), and other [landforms](/wiki/Landform "Landform"). The elevation of the land surface varies from a low point of −418 m (−1,371 ft) at the [Dead Sea](/wiki/Dead_Sea "Dead Sea"), to a maximum altitude of 8,848 m (29,029 ft) at the top of [Mount Everest](/wiki/Mount_Everest "Mount Everest"). The mean height of land above sea level is about 797 m (2,615 ft).[[127]](#cite_note-135) The submarine terrain of the ocean floor has an average [bathymetric](/wiki/Bathymetric "Bathymetric") depth of 4 km, and is as varied as the terrain above sea level.

"We labored the last six months on *Titanic* in the absolute knowledge that the studio would lose $100 million.
